subject: How to highlight the tree linking scattered tips in a large phylogeny?

messages.author: bbd4b13b3cf07e14
messages.subject: How to highlight the tree linking scattered tips in a large phylogeny?
parts:
If I have a large phylogeny of (say) 100 tips, of which, say, 10 are of interest, but which don't form a clade, is there an easy way to use ggtree to plot the 100-tip phylogeny in black by default, but with the branches leading to the 10 focal tips in red? How would I specify the tips in this case?

Thanks if anyone has any suggestions. I'm new to ggplot.

messages.author: bbd4b13b3cf07e14
messages.subject: Re: How to highlight the tree linking scattered tips in a large phylogeny?

Sorry - just found it in the (oddly named) tree manipulation docs: I just use groupOTU() 

https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/treeManipulation.html#group-otus
